name: Real Power (DC)
meaning:
Power delivered to a resistive load.

P = Real power (Watts, W)
V = Voltage (Volts, V)
I = Current (Amperes, A)
R = Resistance (Ohms, Ω)

name: AC Real Power
meaning:
Average power consumed by an AC circuit.

P = Real power (Watts, W)
V = RMS voltage (V)
I = RMS current (A)
θ = Phase angle between V and I

name: Reactive Power
meaning:
Power stored and returned by inductors/capacitors — does no real work.

Q = Reactive power (VAR)
V = RMS voltage (V)
I = RMS current (A)
θ = Phase angle between V and I

name: Apparent Power
meaning:
Total power supplied by the source; combination of real and reactive power.

S = Apparent power (VA)
P = Real power (W)
Q = Reactive power (VAR)
V, I = RMS voltage and current

name: Power Factor
meaning:
Ratio of real power to apparent power; how efficiently power is used.

PF = Power factor (dimensionless, 0–1)
P = Real power (W)
S = Apparent power (VA)
θ = Phase angle between V and I

name: 3-Phase Real Power
meaning:
Real power in a balanced 3-phase system.

P = Total real power (W)
VL = Line-to-line RMS voltage (V)
IL = Line RMS current (A)
θ = Phase angle per phase

name: 3-Phase Apparent Power
meaning:
Total apparent power in a balanced 3-phase system.

S = Apparent power (VA)
VL = Line-to-line RMS voltage (V)
IL = Line RMS current (A)

name: Transformer Power
meaning:
In an ideal transformer, input power equals output power.

V1, V2 = Primary/secondary voltage (V)
I1, I2 = Primary/secondary current (A)
N1, N2 = Primary/secondary turns
Turns ratio: N₁/N₂ = V₁/V₂ = I₂/I₁

name: Joule's Heating Law
meaning:
Heat energy dissipated in a resistor over time.

W = Energy (Joules, J)
P = Power (Watts, W)
I = Current (A)
R = Resistance (Ω)
t = Time (seconds, s)

name: Maximum Power Transfer
meaning:
Maximum power delivered to a load when load resistance equals source resistance.

Pmax = Maximum power (W)
Vs = Thevenin voltage (V)
Rs = Thevenin resistance (Ω)
Condition: RL = Rs
